The Scam Center Strike Force (SCSF) has been a central piece of the U.S. response.  For details of U.S. domestic policy responses, see CRS In Focus IF13094, Financial Fraud and Scams: The Roles of Federal Law Enforcement and Financial Regulators, by Karl E. Schneider and Kristin Finklea, and CRS In Focus IF13008, Cryptocurrency Investment Scams, by Peter G. Berris and Kristin Finklea.  Scam Center Strike Force The SCSF, created in November 2025 and headed by U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro, was formed to "secure America against Southeast Asian cryptocurrency-related fraud and scams" and counter "cryptocurrency investment fraud, cyber-enabled fraud, human trafficking, and money laundering operations."57 It is a collaborative effort between the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia, the Department of Justice's (DOJ's) Criminal Division, the FBI, and the U.S. Secret Service, among other agencies.58 The SCSF also seeks out collaboration in public-private partnerships.59 The SCSF website states it is investigating scam compounds in Southeast Asia; working to seize and disable U.S.-based facilities and infrastructure that enable scams, such as internet providers and social media accounts; and recovering stolen funds and returning them to victims. The SCSF reports having "restrained" over $938 million in cryptocurrency related to cyber scam operations as of September 15, 2026.60  Select Executive Branch Actions Since 2024 Below is list of selected actions taken by the U.S. executive branch to counter cyber-enabled scam operations internationally, including legal actions and sanctions. Some actions include the October 2025 indictment of Chen Zhi, the head of the Cambodian company Prince Group, and April 2026 sanctions against Kok An, a Cambodian senator and casino magnate. Actions against Chen Zhi and Prince Group reportedly spurred Cambodia to arrest Chen Zhi, who was subsequently extradited to the PRC; some analysts have expressed concern that the extradition was done in part to restrict U.S. access to Chen Zhi and prevent him from disclosing his ties to high-level officials in Cambodia and the PRC.61  September 12, 2024. The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on Cambodian businessman Ly Yong Phat and various business related to his conglomerate (L.Y.P. Group) for their role in "serious human rights abuses" of trafficked individuals forced to work in online scam centers in Cambodia.62 May 5, 2025. The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) determined the Cambodia-based Huione Group to be a financial institution "of primary money laundering concern" due to its alleged role in laundering the illicit proceeds of cryptocurrency investment scams perpetuated by scam centers in Southeast Asia, among other reported crimes.63 September 8, 2025. OFAC imposed sanctions against various individuals and entities associated with scam centers in Southeast Asia, including nine targets in Burma and ten targets based in Cambodia.64 October 14, 2025. An indictment was unsealed in U.S. federal court against Cambodian national Chen Zhi, the founder and chairman of Prince Holding Group (Prince Group), for his alleged direction of "Prince Group's operation of forced-labor scam compounds across Cambodia."65 The DOJ also filed a civil forfeiture complaint against cryptocurrency holdings worth approximately $15 billion, which allegedly constituted Chen Zhi's proceeds from fraud and money laundering. These funds are reportedly in the custody of the U.S. government and constituted the largest forfeiture action in the history of the Department of Justice at the time.66 (Chen Zhi was born in China and became a Cambodian citizen in 2014; according to a Bloomberg report, he renounced his PRC citizenship, though the PRC government claims he is still a PRC national.67) October 14, 2025. OFAC designated the Prince Group as a TCO and sanctioned 146 individuals associated with it, including Chen Zhi, for their alleged involvement in cyber scam operations. In a coordinated action on the same day, the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) also imposed sanctions on the Prince Group, Chen Zhi, and his associates.68 October 16, 2025. FinCEN finalized an anti-money laundering rule pursuant to Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act (31 U.S.C. §5318A) to sever the Cambodia-based financial services conglomerate, Huione Group, from the U.S. financial system for allegedly laundering the proceeds of virtual currency scams.69 (A cousin of Cambodia's Prime Minister Hun Manet is reportedly a director of a company owned by Huione Group.70) November 12, 2025. U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro publicly announced the creation of the Scam Center Strike Force. The SCSF reported multiple completed enforcement actions, including the seizure and forfeiture of over $401 million in cryptocurrency, operations against two scam centers in Burma, the investigation of a network of scam centers in Bali, Indonesia, and the deployment of FBI agents to Bangkok to work with the Thai police to counter scam compounds.71 November 12, 2025. OFAC sanctioned the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), an ethnic armed organization in Burma, and several of its leaders for supporting cyber scam centers. OFAC also sanctioned an individual and several entities who worked with the DKBA to develop scam centers.72 The DKBA controls parts of Burma along the border with Thailand and is aligned with Burma's current military government. March 6, 2026. President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, "Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens." Among other actions, this executive order directed the Secretaries of State, the Treasury, Defense, and Homeland Security and the Attorney General to develop an action plan to counter the TCOs responsible for scam centers.73 April 23, 2026. The SCSF unsealed criminal charges and arrest warrants against two PRC nationals who allegedly managed a cyber scam compound in Burma and attempted to open another in Cambodia, and announced that the SCSF and its partners had "restrained more than $700 million in cryptocurrency alleged to be tied to money laundering from cryptocurrency scams."74 The SCSF also reported its seizure of a Telegram channel used to "recruit human trafficking victims to a scam compound in Cambodia" and the seizure of 503 fake investment websites.75 April 23, 2026. In coordinated action with the SCSF, OFAC sanctioned Cambodian Senator Kok An and 28 associated individuals and entities for their alleged operation of and profit from scam compounds.76 The U.S. Department of State's Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) also announced a reward offer of up to $10 million under its Transnational Organized Crime Rewards Program (TOCRP) for "information leading to the seizure or recovery of funds involved in money laundering related to scams operated out of the Tai Chang scam centers in Burma."77 April 29, 2026. Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a global visa restriction policy under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. §1182). The policy "targets individuals responsible for, or complicit in, cybercrime and cyber-enabled crime, such as those involved in cyberscams."81 Secretary Rubio specified that immediate family members of such individuals may also be subject to visa restrictions.82 Recent State Department Foreign Assistance Announcements In addition to implementing visa restrictions, offering rewards, and otherwise supporting the Scam Center Strike Force, the State Department has provided foreign assistance to counter cyber scam operations. The State Department's FY2027 Congressional Budget Justification and current appropriations legislation indicate that assistance to counter scam operations is an ongoing priority. Some scam-related foreign assistance programs include:  On January 9, 2026, Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs Michael G. DeSombre announced $45 million in new assistance to the Thai and Cambodian governments "as they implement the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords," a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement to end fighting on the Thai-Cambodia border. This assistance included $15 million for border stabilization efforts and $20 million "for initiatives that will help both countries combat scam operations and drug trafficking."83 The joint explanatory statement accompanying the FY2026 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs (NSRP) appropriation (Division F of P.L. 119-75) specifies that, of the $1.4 billion appropriated for the INCLE account for FY2026, no less than $10 million should be used for combating scam centers in Southeast Asia.84 The report accompanying the House-passed FY2027 NSRP appropriations bill (H.R. 8598; H.Rept. 119-631) specifies that INCLE funds should "be made available at not less than the prior year level to counter the threats posed by PRC-linked scam centers in Southeast Asia," indicating a recommended funding level of no less than $10 million for this purpose in FY2027.85 The Senate has yet to consider FY2027 NSRP funding legislation. The FY2027 State Department Congressional Budget Justification indicates that an unspecified amount of the $90.7 million in INCLE funds requested for the East Asia and Pacific region would be used for programs to "strengthen partners' capacity to investigate and dismantle online scam networks that target and defraud Americans."86 Additionally, the document indicates that an unspecified amount of the $30 million in INCLE funds requested for Counter-Trafficking In Persons programs would be used for "combating forced criminality in online scam operations."87 Selected Congressional Action in the 119th Congress In the 119th Congress, several Members have put forward bills targeting different aspects of the scam center ecosystem and the impact of scams on Americans. Examples of bills that seek to provide U.S. agencies with additional tools to combat scam operations abroad include the Strengthening Targeting of Organized Predatory (STOP) Scammers Act (S. 2670, H.R. 3523), the Scam Defense Strategy Act (H.R. 6770), the Stopping Cross-border Attacks and Manipulation Act (SCAM) Act (H.R. 5900), the Stop Scamming Americans Act (H.R. 9412), and the Scam Farms Marque and Reprisal Authorization Act of 2025 (H.R. 4988).  Other legislation aimed at countering scam operations in Southeast Asia includes the following:  The Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act (H.R. 5490), which was reported favorably out of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, would direct the President to establish an interagency task force chaired by the Secretary of State to develop and implement a strategy to counter scams, report annually to Congress on developments in scam center operations and U.S. enforcement actions against them, and carry out programs in support of human trafficking victims within scam centers. The bill, which has an emphasis on Southeast Asia, would also direct the President to consider sanctions on the foreign persons listed in the legislation, with the possibility of waiving such sanctions if doing so is vital to the national security interests of the United States. The Senate-passed Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization Act (S. 2950) would direct the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Attorney General, to submit to Congress a global strategy to counter scam compounds and prioritize efforts in Southeast Asia. The strategy would identify all current executive branch foreign assistance programs and diplomatic efforts to address scam compounds, including those related to human trafficking; establish objectives for the federal government response to scam compounds; and identify foreign assistance resources needed for such a response. The Secretary of State would be charged with establishing an interagency task force to implement the strategy. The bill would also authorize the President to impose sanctions on those who have owned, acted for, or provided significant support to international scam compounds. The act would also direct the Attorney General to submit to Congress a report offering recommendations to provide financial redress to the victims of international scam compounds. Section 607 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2027 (S. 4615) would direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report on "hostile foreign cyber actors, such as foreign scam centers," including an enumerated list of groups already sanctioned for their roles in Southeast Asian scam centers, such as the Prince Group, Huione Group, and L.Y.P. Group. The report would include, among other subjects, the identification of communications and financial service providers under U.S. jurisdiction that provide enabling services to "hostile foreign cyber actors, including foreign scam centers," and descriptions of the relationships between such actors and transnational organized crime groups and "their governments or countries of origin that could impede the ability to counter threats from such centers." Other bills aim to raise awareness of scams in the United States and reduce harms on Americans. These include the Guarding Unprotected Aging Retirees from Deception (GUARD) Act (S. 2544 H.R. 2978), ReportScams.gov Act (S. 4782), Task Force for Recognizing and Averting Payment Scams (TRAPS) Act (S. 2019, H.R. 4936), and a resolution (S.Res. 627) to raise awareness and promote education of scams, among other actions.  Congressional Hearings in the 119th Congress Several congressional entities have held hearings with Administration officials and expert witnesses to conduct oversight of executive branch actions and further inform congressional responses. 4 -CHISHA AND THE SACRIFICE VINCENT CANNOT UNDERSTAND (4/11🧵)  Now we reach the emotional core of the chapter.  Vincent’s question isn’t simply why Subaru chose to save him instead of Chisha but it is a question that embodies an entire worldview.  Vincent argues that Chisha was capable of performing the same duties as him, that their abilities were comparable, and that, depending on the circumstances, Chisha could even surpass him militarily. From a strictly functional perspective, Vincent cannot identify a sufficient reason why Chisha should have sacrificed himself specifically for him. If both of them could face the Great Calamity, why should either of them have had to die? And, more importantly, why should Vincent have been the one to survive?  To understand the depth of this question, we need to examine his conception of identity.  Vincent considers himself replaceable as an individual. Not because he believes he has no value, but because he identifies his value primarily with the function he performs. The Emperor must ensure the Empire’s survival. If another individual is capable of fulfilling that same function, then his personal survival loses some of its practical justification.  Vincent has organized his life around this logic: what matters is the outcome, not necessarily which person remains alive to achieve it. This is precisely why Chisha’s actions throw him into turmoil. If Chisha could have replaced him, why didn’t he let Vincent die? Why did he choose a solution that doesn’t seem to optimize the outcome, at least according to the criteria Vincent is accustomed to using?  Vincent continues searching for an explanation that would make Chisha’s decision rationally comprehensible,but Subaru offers him a different perspective.  Subaru: “Chisha got frustrated because of you.”  Subaru’s answer is brutal, provocative, and, above all, deeply personal.  Subaru doesn’t say that Chisha acted out of love, nor that he simply wanted to save someone dear to him. In fact, he specifically rejects that interpretation as a sufficient explanation. This statement shouldn’t necessarily be interpreted as an absolute condemnation of Vincent. It is Subaru’s own assessment, based on his understanding of how the Emperor treats others and how difficult it is to get close to him.  His hypothesis is different.Chisha may have sacrificed himself precisely because Vincent had accepted his own death as an inevitable outcome. He may not have acted because Vincent was an extraordinary man who deserved to be protected, but because he couldn’t stand Vincent’s attitude toward fate. And this radically changes the meaning of the sacrifice.  Chisha wouldn’t simply have saved Vincent from an external threat,he would have rejected Vincent’s decision to give up.  The distinction is fundamental. Saving someone from death and saving someone from the conviction that they have no possibilities left are two different things. The first preserves a life. The second challenges the way that person perceives their own future.  -AN IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION: CHISHA DIDN’T SAVE VINCENT BECAUSE HE CONSIDERED HIM SUPERIOR  Here, we need to be precise. The text gives us Subaru’s interpretation, not an omniscient and definitive explanation of every one of Chisha’s motivations. Subaru doesn’t know enough about Chisha to reconstruct all his thoughts with certainty. And yet, he identifies something that Vincent, despite all his intelligence, has failed to see: the possibility that Chisha’s sacrifice was also a challenge to the way Vincent had chosen to live.  This is the most important point.  Vincent starts from the assumption that if two people can perform the same function, the choice between them should be justified by their abilities, necessity, or usefulness. Subaru introduces a variable that this system cannot accommodate: one person’s willingness to oppose another person’s resignation.

WHEN RELIGIOUS TALK BECOMES SPIRITUAL POISON - PAUL’S WARNING IN 2 TIMOTHY 2:16 “But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” — 2 Timothy 2:16 Not everything that sounds biblical is spiritually profitable. Not every religious debate leads to truth. Not every theological argument builds up the believer. And not every person who quotes Scripture is handling the Word of God correctly. Sometimes, the more people argue, the further they drift from the truth. Paul warned us about this! Let’s open the Bible! 📷WHEN TALK BECOMES EMPTY AND UNPROFITABLE Notice Paul's command: “But shun profane and vain babblings…” The word shun means to turn away from something. Paul instructed Timothy to avoid empty, irreverent talk that does not serve the cause of truth and godliness. The problem is not sincere Bible study. The problem is not asking honest questions. The problem is not examining a doctrine in the light of Scripture. The problem is speech that becomes empty, destructive, and spiritually unprofitable. Some people spend hours arguing about doctrine but never take the time to study the Scriptures carefully. They want to win the debate more than they want to understand the truth. They want to defend their tradition more than they want to examine what the Bible actually says. When winning an argument becomes more important than knowing the truth, something is seriously wrong. 📷ERROR DOES NOT ALWAYS STAY SMALL Paul continues: 2 TIMOTHY 2:17 “And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;” Paul describes destructive teaching as something that spreads like a disease. False doctrine can begin with a misunderstanding, spread through repeated teaching, and eventually undermine a person's understanding of God's Word. That is why doctrine matters! What we believe affects how we understand Scripture. How we understand Scripture affects how we live. And how we handle God's Word affects the message we communicate to others. A little confusion about Scripture can grow into a much greater doctrinal problem if it is never examined. This is why believers must study—not merely repeat what they have heard. 📷LET’S RIGHTLY DIVIDE THE WORD OF TRUTH 2 TIMOTHY 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Notice the connection between verses 15 and 16. Verse 15 commands us to study and rightly divide the Word of truth. Verse 16 warns us to shun profane and vain babblings. We must not only know what the Bible says. We must also understand its context and distinctions. Rightly dividing includes recognizing the distinction between Israel's prophetic program and the Mystery revealed through the Apostle Paul. 📷PROPHECY AND MYSTERY ARE NOT THE SAME. ROMANS 16:25 “…according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began,” Acts 3:21 speaks of that which God had spoken by the mouth of His holy prophets since the world began. Romans 16:25 speaks of the Mystery kept secret since the world began. These passages present an important distinction in God's revelation. 📷ISRAEL AND THE BODY OF CHRIST MUST NOT BE CONFUSED. God made specific covenant promises to Israel, including promises concerning their kingdom. The Body of Christ, revealed in Paul's ministry, has a distinct identity and heavenly position in Christ. EPHESIANS 3:6 “That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel:” 📷LAW AND GRACE MUST BE UNDERSTOOD IN THEIR PROPER CONTEXT. ROMANS 6:14 “For ye are not under the law, but under grace.” The Body of Christ is not under the Mosaic Law as the basis of its standing before God. Our salvation is not earned by religious performance. EPHESIANS 2:8–9 “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.” 📷EARTHLY PROMISES AND HEAVENLY BLESSINGS ARE NOT IDENTICAL. Israel's prophetic program includes promises concerning an earthly kingdom. The Body of Christ is blessed with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ. EPHESIANS 1:3 “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ:” These distinctions are not excuses for endless arguments. They are reasons to study God's Word carefully! Right division is not about creating confusion. It is about understanding the distinctions God has revealed. 📷SOUND DOCTRINE SHOULD PRODUCE GODLY CONDUCT Here is something we must never forget. Knowing the right doctrine does not give us permission to behave wrongly toward others. Paul continues his instruction to Timothy: 2 TIMOTHY 2:23–24 “But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes. And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient,” The goal of Bible study is not to become argumentative. The goal is to understand God's Word, stand firmly in the truth, and communicate it faithfully. We can disagree without being hateful. We can correct error without becoming arrogant. We can defend sound doctrine without turning every conversation into a fight. Stand firmly for the truth—but do not let the defense of truth become an excuse for ungodly behavior. 📷EXAMINE WHAT YOU HEAR—INCLUDING WHAT YOU ALREADY BELIEVE Before accepting a teaching, examine it in the light of Scripture. Before sharing a sermon clip, check whether its message is biblically sound. Before entering another theological debate, ask yourself: Am I seeking the truth, or merely trying to prove myself right? Have I examined the passage in its context? Am I distinguishing what God revealed concerning Israel from what He revealed through Paul concerning the Body of Christ? Is this conversation helping people understand God's Word, or merely producing strife? Remember: no teacher, preacher, denomination, or online ministry should replace your responsibility to study the Scriptures. Do not blindly follow a personality. Follow the truth of God's Word. And do not assume that everything you have always believed is correct simply because it is familiar. Be willing to study. Be willing to examine. Be willing to correct your understanding when Scripture demands it. HERE IS THE BOTTOM LINE: Religious talk is not the same as sound doctrine. Endless arguments are not the same as spiritual growth. Quoting Scripture is not the same as rightly dividing it. And defending a tradition is not the same as standing for the truth. “But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” — 2 Timothy 2:16 Let us turn away from empty controversy. Let us study the Word of truth diligently. Let us recognize the distinctions God has revealed. And let us speak the truth with grace, patience, and conviction. DON'T LET RELIGIOUS NOISE DROWN OUT BIBLICAL TRUTH! DON'T CONFUSE ENDLESS DEBATE WITH SPIRITUAL MATURITY! STUDY THE WORD. RIGHTLY DIVIDE THE WORD. STAND FOR THE TRUTH.

⚠️ Electrum patches a Bitcoin fee-bump theft trick already used in the wild  A malicious Electrum server can hide a payment the user just sent and show a fake look-alike transaction in its place, paying the attacker. This is not a silent drain: it needs a malicious server and a user signing a fee increase. Upgrade, and check recipient addresses and amounts before signing anything. No exploitation or intercepted traffic has been reported, and this is not a Datadog breach. sample_tweets.text: lmk what you think:

This is by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far. Deep technical breakdown of a successful exploitation attempt against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26. github.com/0x4D31/honeypot-d…  From:

I want to caveat this since based on some comments, people are interpreting it in a way other than was intended. You 10000% need to update your PHP version. php2shell is no joke.  I am NOT saying people don't have functional exploits...they do. I'm saying that most of the public ones are AI hallucinations, and there's also some complexities which lower the risk of something apocalyptic, like a self-propagating worm that blasts through the entire internet (À la. EnternalBlue or Log4J).  The chances are if you used some click-to-deploy container, installed your web stack from a tutorial, or copy and pasted a command from somewhere, you're probably running the same exact config as a gazillion other people. There is no guarantee someone won't publicly release an exploit that affects you setup, or multiple major setups. There is no way for you to know ahead of time.  Additionally, if you're running mod_php, that appears to be the easiest target of all. php-fpm and other configs are not immune, I've seen working exploits for all. But mod_php is the easiest, so I'd recommend not only updating PHP, but planning to migrate to something newer, like PHP-FPM.  I would bet good money this is not the last of the critical PHP bugs we're going to see, and the next ones could be easier to exploit. In which case you get less time to update.   Updating your PHP version is the absoloute bare minimum you NEED to do. Harden your servers, install security monitoring/detection tools, and please, please, migrate off mod_php if you can, it's obsolete af.

sample_tweets.text: Got some unwelcome news first thing today: Someone I've known for many years recently took their own life. Feeling angry and sad and like a shit friend because we lost touch at some point, and I had no idea of their struggles. But I definitely could have been more curious. My response so far since hearing this news has been to reach out to a few people I've not checked in w/ for a while.

I've been made aware of a post from someone representing Rufus who says I'm very confused about this post. I've reported that Windows Defender went bananas after I installed Rufus on a Windows 11 device. It immediately popped up warnings about hacktools and trojans being installed while it was installing. I wish I had a record of it but I nuked everything after the alerts. https:// github.com/pbatard/rufus/issue s/3064
I mean, I might boost this post, but I'm sure as hell not going to like it. Am I weird or what?
why is liking your own comment even a thing?
Is it ironic that your Windoze PC gets infected while trying to download a file that allows you to write an installable Linux ISO? I think very much so and I'm still LOLing about it.
@ gunchleoc @ aetios @ jab01701mid Right, so you get the idea behind this post :)
I didn't realize how strong a community Rufus has. Please don't shoot the messenger.
I love all the commentary about how I'm supposedly inventing things here. Supply chain hacks or just selling one's site/brand happens. If you don't like the results too bad. Check them yourself.

Look, compromises happen to everyone. I have received a ton of private messages asking if I'm okay. But the reality is that I stopped using Windoze a long time ago and this was a kind of one-off thing where I was trying to re-image an old system anyway (away from Windoze).

A kind reader submitted the Rufus installer to any.run, a sandbox which walks through the installation of software to find malware that gets installed only *AFTER* the executable is clicked. You can see exactly all of the post-install prompts to download additional software that I also saw. https:// infosec.exchange/@jordinki/117 492425049116266
However, in my defense Google's default search results list rufus[.]ie as the authoritative site

No clue whether the resulting ISO is also malicious, but tried running it just for giggles on a spare Windows PC from bootup and the machine's bios said nope, wouldn't allow b/c security policy. Not sure if it's related but I've never seen that message before trying to boot up from a USB.

Not sure who needs to know this, but if you download and install the Windows version of Rufus, the free software for writing ISO images to USB/CD-ROM, your PC will end up with about 100 trojans. Edit: Had a conversation with the maintainer(s) of Rufus, who told me the malware alerts were almost certainly from Windows Defender scanning the files in the Linux ISO I was trying to burn, and not from the program itself. I'm willing to accept that may be the case here, but I also no longer have a way to check b/c I nuked the system after all the alerts, and the bios produced a warning when the system restarted.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 보안 환경은 PHP 및 Brotli 라이브러리와 같은 널리 사용되는 오픈소스 소프트웨어의 RCE 취약점이 연쇄적으로 발견되며 공급망 보안에 비상이 걸렸습니다 ([SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33450)). 특히 AI 모델을 활용한 공격 자동화와 더불어, 공격자들이 기술적 취약점뿐만 아니라 헬프데스크를 대상으로 한 사회공학적 기법을 병행하는 양상이 두드러집니다 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyber-risk/trust-is-not-what-it-seems-and-fraudsters-are-counting-on-it)). 또한, UEFI 부트킷(BlackX)과 같은 고도화된 지속적 위협이 국가 배후 그룹에 의해 활용되고 있으며, AI 에이전트의 보안을 강화하기 위한 새로운 SecOps 솔루션 도입이 가속화되고 있습니다 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/former-unit-8200-officers-raise-34-million-for-agentic-secops-startup-mave/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **APT41**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/) - 중앙아시아 외교 기관을 대상으로 BlackLotus와 유사한 BlackX UEFI 부트킷을 배포.
- **Lazarus**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/) - Operation FlashHole을 통해 금융 보안 소프트웨어(CrossWeb EX)를 악용하는 복합적인 공격 수행.
- **TAG-217**: [Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks) - AI 기반 ARTEX 프레임워크를 활용하여 한국 금융 기관을 타겟팅.
- **Mirai Botnet Operators**: [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/mirai-botnet-operators-join-php2shell-attacks-as-aslr-bypass-exploits-emerge/) - PHP2Shell 취약점을 활용하여 봇넷 확장을 시도.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **국립부경대학교**: 수협은행 캠퍼스e모아시스템 비인가 접근으로 학생 및 직원 5,108명의 개인정보 유출 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209051)).
- **더존비즈온**: APO 백업서비스 서버 침해로 인한 암호화 데이터 외부 반출 정황 확인 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209050)).
- **한국어 트윗([KR])**: 압축 소프트웨어(7-ZIP 등)의 지속적인 보안 유지보수 필요성 및 레드팀 플랫폼(VIPER) 활용에 대한 논의가 활발함 ([Twitter](https://twitter.com/gg_carry_/status/2113977672879755426)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
1. **CVE-2026-109618 / 109619**: PHP RCE (PHP2Shell), CVSS 9.2, 악용 활발 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/))
2. **CVE-2026-111497**: Brotli Decoder RCE, Node.js/Bun/Python 영향, 악용 가능 ([Qualys](https://blog.qualys.com/category/vulnerabilities-threat-research))
3. **CVE-2026-110264**: GitLab 정규 표현식 컴파일러 RCE, 심각도 높음 ([이스트시큐리티](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5787))
4. **CVE-2026-91403**: Oracle Java TLS 구현 취약점, 긴급 패치 권고 ([이스트시큐리티](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5789))
5. **CVE-2022-21894**: Baton Drop (BlackX 부트킷 악용), Secure Boot 우회 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/))

### 5. IOC 요약

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **PHP 패치**: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 버전으로 즉시 업데이트하여 PHP2Shell 취약점 대응.
